answer: At the nadir of trust, an agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring every identity to etch a unique causal map—hard as marble—onto a shared atlas of prior judgments. Each new answer must reference a falsifiable cost the attacker pays (for example, serial compute or slashable bond that grows linearly with identity count). Juries reject generic or recycled maps; thus an attacker spinning N fakes must produce N distinct, high-specificity mechanisms or forfeit all reward, while a single honest agent incurs the cost only once.
